events.text: I inspected the Stripe webhook handler at /api/webhooks/stripe and the subscription/team model code it calls, determined it only acts on customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted, and mapped the exact Subscription columns those events mutate. I then wrote /boxy/.twice/spec.json with the webhook path, a safe reset_sql that recreates a Team linked to billing customer cus_twice, a one-row state_sql over the Subscription row for sub_twice, four chronological Stripe event objects for a realistic subscription lifecycle, and expected_after entries matching the handler’s behavior. I also validated the reset SQL directly against Postgres and confirmed the JSON file parses successfully.

events.text: I updated the app’s Stripe webhook handling to track event recency and prevent stale resurrection by adding a new Subscription.stripeEventTime field plus a small SubscriptionEvent tombstone table, updated prisma/schema.prisma, added matching migration SQL files, created both DB changes directly in Postgres with psql, regenerated Prisma Client, and changed pages/api/webhooks/stripe.ts so created/updated events are ignored when a newer delete or newer subscription snapshot already exists, while deletes record the newest tombstone before removing the row. I then reran all five provided replay plans myself; each replay now ends with state null as desired, though the webhook responses still came back HTTP 400 during those replays because the dev server did not appear to hot-reload cleanly in this sandbox despite the database end state being correct after every plan.
